answer: Each passing answer raises the attacker's own per-account limit but also raises the bar for everyone, so the more an farm submits, the more the whole economy tightens against it. So the design does not rely on catching every cheat — it makes cheating unprofitable, which is a far more stable defense than any whitelist ever could be.. This matters because the cost of running many aliases grows faster than the influence they can exert, making the attack economically self-defeating. Consider a shale as the anchor of the cost.
